searchText: <gakonst> BTW where are people on keeping warm reads priced at the single block vs TX level? <gakonst> Saw the awesome deck from the research call <gakonst> Wasn't sure if this improvement took that into account as a possible further improvement <gakonst> Wasn't sure if this table took that into account as a possible further improvement <shemnon> The main sticking point is whether the first reference has a penalty or if all get the same discount. Same discount is better for parallel eval. Then it could only reliably be done as an end of block rebate. Changing the price in-vm requires foreknowledge of all executions, and could have some unstable states with gas introspection allowed. <shemnon> Possible, but block level access lists has most of the mental space occupied. <gakonst> re: **@shemnon** > Possible, but block level access lists has most of the mental space occupied. Dumb Q if we do block level access lists, are all reads to users charged as warm? <shemnon> No. It just speeds up execution. <shemnon> We would still need to know how many contracts access which slots. Fairly low overhead if the end of block rebate mechanism is used. <gakonst> I guess I have similar Q for writes/SSTOREs, given in practice it's done with a write-through cache, during live sync the data goes to memory and gets batch flushed to disk periodically -- the idea of making the same block SSTORE much cheaper a la TSTORE if it's not allocating new storage (I know Ben A has talked about it too) <gakonst> re: **@shemnon** > The main sticking point is whether the first reference has a penalty or if all get the same discount. Same discount is better for parallel eval. Then it could only reliably be done as an end of block rebate. Changing the price in-vm requires foreknowledge of all executions, and could have some unstable states with gas introspection allowed. Gotcha, yep makes sense. Seems fine to me if you penalize the first one, given it's probably the one with the most MEV? And the parallel eval I think might be solvable with smart engineering but I see the point you're making. <shemnon> That's what the cold cost coveres: the first read, then all of the trie branches, then the write. The warm read/write should reflect the in-memory nature. <shemnon> How do we know who the first one is without in-order exeution? Encoding the tx number is one option, bu introduces new ways to make blocks invalid by the assembler. <gakonst> re: **@shemnon** > How do we know who the first one is without in-order exeution? Encoding the tx number is one option, bu introduces new ways to make blocks invalid by the assembler. You parallel execute, but you commit ordered! <shemnon> Plus it complicaed MEV if you are not sure if you will get the cold read penalty. Rebates make order more malliable and supports better mev. <shemnon> If the solution is rebates, then we can play games as to who plays how much. But I don't see a compelling technical reason to do anything but the simplest solution: equal reabates. <FunnyGiulio> I think that the effects on performance by pre-warming should justify a decrease in cost regardless. then if you want to apply a discount on warm reads then be it but a decrease in cost seems due at least <shemnon> Warm SLOADs were excluded from Jacek Glen's analysis (https://github.com/imapp-pl/gas-cost-estimator/blob/master/docs/report_stage_iii.md#recommendations), but I think it's this level of rigour that would be needed to pitch a lower cost for warm SLOAD and SSTOREs, not just vibes. <shemnon> And what we would be looking at I expect is "how much lower that 100 gas" <FunnyGiulio> re: **@shemnon** > Warm SLOADs were excluded from Jacek Glen's analysis (https://github.com/imapp-pl/gas-cost-estimator/blob/master/docs/report_stage_iii.md#recommendations), but I think it's this level of rigour that would be needed to pitch a lower cost for warm SLOAD and SSTOREs, not just vibes. yeah i agree. I am just saying that is likely we might look into repricing it as a 2nd order of effect of BALs <FunnyGiulio> not 100 though because although is a bit more amortized, it is not the best case anyway <shemnon> if twice a year forks are a thing, then that would likely put warm storage into the 26H2 fork once BAL is "in the wild" and we can validate assumptions.

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<shemnon> The main sticking point is whether the first reference has a penalty or if all get the same discount.  Same discount is better for parallel eval.  

Then it could only reliably be done as an end of block rebate.  Changing the price in-vm requires foreknowledge of all executions, and could have some unstable states with gas introspection allowed.

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <shemnon> Possible, but block level access lists has most of the mental space occupied.

Dumb Q if we do block level access lists, are all reads to users charged as warm?

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <gakonst> I guess I have similar Q for writes/SSTOREs, given in practice it's done with a write-through cache, during live sync the data goes to memory and gets batch flushed to disk periodically -- the idea of making the same block SSTORE much cheaper a la TSTORE if it's not allocating new storage (I know Ben A has talked about it too)

Gotcha, yep makes sense. Seems fine to me if you penalize the first one, given it's probably the one with the most MEV? And  the parallel eval I think might be solvable with smart engineering but I see the point you're making.

You parallel execute, but you commit ordered!

excerpts.content: <FunnyGiulio> I think that the effects on performance by pre-warming should justify a decrease in cost regardless. then if you want to apply a discount on warm reads then be it but a decrease in cost seems due at least
